In summary, our research is concerned with
the multiple parton scattering and the induced parton energy losses in DIS off heavy nuclei within the framework of perturbative QED and QCD.
the study of the nuclear effects in the Drell-Yan process.
the multiple parton scattering in the nuclear medium and its effects on the parton energy loss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the induced energy loss in DIS on a nucleus is reduced by a factor (1+1/6) compared with the result of the soft gluon approximation.
the parton energy loss due to multiple scattering is not as large as previously estimated.
the parton energy loss induced by multiple scattering in nuclei is significantly smaller than the one estimated by the helicity amplitude approximation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multiple parton scattering in heavy nuclei is reduced by a factor 2/3 from that in the case of helicity amplitude (soft bremsstrahlglung) approximation.

the induced parton energy losses for both DIS and jet tomography can be significantly reduced by a factor between 2/3 and 5/6, depending on the kinematical conditions, if the multiple scattering is taken into account beyond the helicity-amplitude approximation.
the parton energy loss induced by the multiple scattering in the nucleus is reduced from the result of soft gluon bremsstrahlungs by the factor of 1/3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multiple parton scattering in the target nucleus is a non-trivial quantum mechanical process and should not be approximated by a simple classical multiple scattering picture.
the induced parton energy losses in DIS and Drell-Yan processes are not the same.
the helicity amplitude approximation should be used with caution when the multiple scattering effect is large.
